desc_a: A commercial business entity that produces or sells goods and services.
desc_b: a commercial business entity that produces or sells goods and services.
rationale: Identical concept, differing only by capitalization.

desc_a: A structured group of people working toward a common purpose.
desc_b: Structured groups of people working toward a common purpose.
rationale: Singular/plural form of the same concept.

desc_a: A machine used for transporting people or goods, typically on roads.
desc_b: Machines used for transporting people or goods, typically on roads.
rationale: Singular/plural form of the same concept.

desc_a: A business primarily engaged in developing or selling technology products.
desc_b: A business primarily engaged in developing or selling technology products and services.
rationale: Abbreviation vs full word, same referent concept.

desc_a: A good or item manufactured or refined for sale.
desc_b: goods or items manufactured or refined for sale.
rationale: Case + plural variant of same concept.

desc_a: A specific place or position in physical space.
desc_b: Specific places or positions in physical space.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: A written, printed, or electronic record used as information or evidence.
desc_b: A written, printed, or electronic record used as information or evidence.
rationale: Leading whitespace only difference.

desc_a: An occurrence or happening, especially one of importance.
desc_b: An occurrence or happening, especially one of importance.
rationale: Case-only variant.

desc_a: A written or printed work consisting of pages bound together.
desc_b: Written or printed works consisting of pages bound together.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: An assembly of people for a particular purpose, especially for discussion.
desc_b: assemblies of people for a particular purpose, especially for discussion.
rationale: Case + plural variant.

desc_a: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.
desc_b: Nations with their own governments, occupying particular territories.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: An institution of higher education and research.
desc_b: Institutions of higher education and research.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: A planned piece of work with a defined goal, undertaken over a period of time.
desc_b: A planned piece of work with a defined goal, undertaken over a period of time.
rationale: Case-only variant.

desc_a: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties.
desc_b: Legally binding agreements between two or more parties.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: A large human settlement, typically with administrative and commercial significance.
desc_b: Large human settlements, typically with administrative and commercial significance.
rationale: Plural variant, same concept.

desc_a: A member of the species Homo sapiens, distinguished from other animals by capacity for abstract thought.
desc_b: A single person considered separately from a group or society.
rationale: Both refer to a single human person; zero shared lexical tokens but same referent in most extraction contexts.

desc_a: A qualified practitioner of medicine who diagnoses and treats illness.
desc_b: A person licensed to practice medicine and treat patients.
rationale: Synonymous professional roles; same real-world concept.

desc_a: A commercial business, especially one providing professional services such as legal or financial advice.
desc_b: A commercial business entity that produces or sells goods and services.
rationale: Both denote a commercial business entity; interchangeable in most contexts.

desc_a: A self-propelled passenger road vehicle with four wheels, powered by an internal combustion or electric engine.
desc_b: A wheeled motor vehicle used for transporting passengers on roads.
rationale: Synonyms for the same passenger road vehicle.

desc_a: A person legally qualified to represent clients in legal matters and act on their behalf.
desc_b: A person who practices law, representing and advising clients on legal matters.
rationale: Near-synonymous legal professional roles.

desc_a: A place where a person lives, especially formally recognized as such.
desc_b: The place where a person lives, often connoting personal or family belonging.
rationale: Both refer to a dwelling place a person lives in.

desc_a: A large company or group of companies authorized to act as a single legal entity.
desc_b: A business or company, especially a large or ambitious one.
rationale: Both refer to a large business organization.

desc_a: The act of buying something.
desc_b: The act of acquiring or gaining possession of something, typically through buying.
rationale: Near-synonymous transaction concepts.

desc_a: A young human being, informally referred to.
desc_b: A young human being below the age of puberty.
rationale: Informal vs formal register for the same age-based person concept.

desc_a: A handwritten or typed composition, especially an author's own copy before publication.
desc_b: A written, printed, or electronic record used as information or evidence.
rationale: Manuscript is a specific instance of the broader document concept; in most entity-type taxonomies these collapse to one type.

desc_a: A person who teaches or trains others, especially in a formal or professional capacity.
desc_b: A person who imparts knowledge or skill to students.
rationale: Near-synonymous roles for a person who educates others.

desc_a: A large body of people united by common descent, history, culture, or language, inhabiting a particular territory.
desc_b: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.
rationale: Near-synonymous concepts for a sovereign territorial entity.

desc_a: Money in physical form, such as coins and banknotes.
desc_b: A system of money in general use in a particular country.
rationale: In many extraction contexts both denote monetary value/medium, treated as the same underlying financial-entity concept.

desc_a: A portable telephone that can make and receive calls without a fixed wired connection.
desc_b: A portable telephone that can make and receive calls over a cellular network.
rationale: Regional synonyms for the same device concept.

desc_a: A group of living organisms consisting of similar individuals capable of interbreeding.
desc_b: Money in the form of coins, as opposed to paper currency.
rationale: Naive lemma stripping ('species' -> 'specie') collapses a biological-taxonomy concept into an unrelated monetary concept; genuinely distinct.

desc_a: The branch of science concerned with the nature and properties of matter and energy.
desc_b: Archaic term for a medicine or remedial treatment, especially a laxative.
rationale: 'Physics' minus trailing 's' yields an archaic medicine term, not the science discipline; distinct concepts.

desc_a: The branch of philosophy dealing with moral principles governing behavior.
desc_b: A set of moral principles held by an individual or group, especially as a personal code of conduct.
rationale: 'Ethics' as an academic discipline differs from 'an ethic' as a specific personal/group value system; distinct granularity of concept.

desc_a: The ratio expressing the probability of an event occurring versus not occurring, especially in betting.
desc_b: A number not divisible evenly by two.
rationale: 'Odds' (probability ratio) is unrelated to 'odd' (a numeric parity property); classic false-lemma-merge trap.

desc_a: Merchandise or possessions, especially items for sale or trade.
desc_b: A morally right or virtuous quality or deed.
rationale: 'Goods' (commercial merchandise) is unrelated to 'good' (moral quality); distinct concepts despite lemma similarity.

desc_a: A government agency and process for controlling the flow of goods, including animals, into and out of a country.
desc_b: A traditional practice or habitual way of behaving specific to a particular society or individual.
rationale: 'Customs' as a border-control institution differs from 'a custom' as a cultural practice; distinct concepts.

desc_a: Weapons, especially firearms, considered collectively.
desc_b: The upper limb of the human body, from shoulder to hand.
rationale: 'Arms' (weaponry) is unrelated to 'arm' (body part); distinct concepts despite shared root spelling.

desc_a: A number of related or similar things, events, or people coming one after another.
desc_b: Not a standard English word; occasionally a mistaken singular back-formation with no established distinct meaning.
rationale: 'Series' is already both singular and plural in English; naive stripping of trailing 's' produces a non-word, illustrating a degenerate lemma-collision failure mode rather than a real synonym.

desc_a: A piece of transparent material with curved surfaces used to focus or diverge light rays, as in a camera or eyeglasses.
desc_b: A given name (short for Leonard or Leonora), used as a person's first name.
rationale: 'Lens' (optical device) is unrelated to 'Len' (a personal name); distinct concepts despite lemma similarity.

desc_a: The method or resources by which a result is achieved, especially financial resources.
desc_b: The average value of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the sum by the count.
rationale: 'Means' (financial resources / method) is unrelated to 'mean' (statistical average); distinct concepts.

desc_a: Newly received or noteworthy information about recent events, especially as reported by media.
desc_b: An adjective describing something recently made, discovered, or created.
rationale: 'News' (reported information) is unrelated to 'new' (an adjective for recency); distinct concepts and word classes.

desc_a: Socially polite behaviors and etiquette expected in a given culture.
desc_b: The way in which a thing is done or happens; a method or style.
rationale: 'Manners' as etiquette is a distinct concept from 'manner' as a general method or style, despite common root.

desc_a: Lodgings or accommodation, especially provided for military personnel.
desc_b: One of four equal parts into which something is divided.
rationale: 'Quarters' (lodging) is unrelated to 'quarter' (a fractional part); distinct concepts despite lemma similarity.

desc_a: The land surrounding a building or estate, or the justification/reason for an action.
desc_b: The solid surface of the earth; also, an electrical connection to the earth.
rationale: 'Grounds' as reasons/land-surrounding-a-building diverges from 'ground' as the earth's surface or an electrical concept; distinct senses.

desc_a: A pair of glasses worn to correct or aid eyesight.
desc_b: A visually striking public performance or display, especially one on a large scale.
rationale: 'Spectacles' (eyewear) is unrelated to 'spectacle' (a dramatic public event); classic distinct-lemma-collision pair.

desc_a: A person's movable personal property or belongings.
desc_b: A change that is a result or consequence of an action or other cause.
rationale: 'Effects' (personal belongings) is unrelated to 'effect' (a causal consequence); distinct concepts despite shared root.

desc_a: A sum of money claimed or awarded in compensation for a loss or injury, especially in a legal context.
desc_b: Physical harm or impairment caused to an object, structure, or person.
rationale: 'Damages' as a legal monetary award differs from 'damage' as physical harm; distinct legal vs physical concepts.

desc_a: A building or land occupied by a business or considered as a place.
desc_b: A statement or proposition from which a conclusion is logically drawn.
rationale: 'Premises' (a physical property) is unrelated to 'premise' (a logical proposition); classic false-friend lemma pair.

desc_a: A factory or industrial site where manufacturing or engineering takes place.
desc_b: Activity involving mental or physical effort done to achieve a purpose or result.
rationale: 'Works' as an industrial site diverges from 'work' as labor/effort in this sense; distinct concepts (though other senses of 'works' do overlap with 'work').

desc_a: A flag or emblem representing a military unit, ship, or nation, carried or displayed with honor.
desc_b: The property of an object producing different sensations on the eye due to the way it reflects light.
rationale: 'Colours' as a military/naval flag is unrelated to 'colour' as a visual property; distinct concepts in this specialized sense.

desc_a: A machine used for transporting people or goods, typically on roads.
desc_b: A set of instructions for preparing a particular dish, including ingredients and method.
rationale: Completely unrelated domains: transportation vs culinary instructions.

desc_a: A human being regarded as an individual.
desc_b: A structure with a roof and walls, such as a house or factory, standing permanently in one place.
rationale: A living human being is unrelated to a physical structure.

desc_a: A liquid intended for drinking, other than plain water, such as juice or wine.
desc_b: A nation with its own government, occupying a particular territory.
rationale: A drink and a sovereign territorial entity share no conceptual overlap.

desc_a: A set of instructions or programs used to operate computers and execute tasks.
desc_b: A large natural elevation of the earth's surface rising abruptly from the surrounding level.
rationale: Digital instructions vs geological landform, entirely unrelated.

desc_a: A document listing goods sent or services rendered, with a statement of the sum due.
desc_b: A living organism that feeds on organic matter, typically able to move and respond to stimuli.
rationale: A financial document is unrelated to a biological organism.

desc_a: An organized series of events, performances, or celebrations, often held annually.
desc_b: A hand tool used for turning screws to fasten or loosen them.
rationale: A cultural event has nothing in common with a physical hand tool.

desc_a: The identification of a disease or condition based on symptoms and examination.
desc_b: A three-dimensional work of art created by carving, modeling, or casting.
rationale: A medical judgment is unrelated to a physical artwork.

desc_a: A large natural stream of water flowing in a channel to the sea or another body of water.
desc_b: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties.
rationale: A geographic feature is unrelated to a legal agreement.

desc_a: A celestial object consisting of ice and dust that develops a glowing tail as it approaches the sun.
desc_b: A person employed for wages or salary by an organization or another individual.
rationale: An astronomical object is unrelated to an employment role.

desc_a: A contract representing an agreement between an insurer and policyholder for financial protection against loss.
desc_b: A rupture in the earth's crust that allows molten rock, ash, and gases to escape.
rationale: A financial contract is unrelated to a geological feature.

desc_a: An organized group of singers, especially one performing in a church or concert.
desc_b: A computer application for organizing, analyzing, and storing data in tabular form.
rationale: A musical ensemble is unrelated to a software application.

desc_a: An official document issued by a government certifying identity and citizenship for international travel.
desc_b: A place where a stream falls, typically from a vertical cliff or rock face.
rationale: A travel document is unrelated to a natural geographic feature.

desc_a: A medicine that destroys or inhibits the growth of bacteria, used to treat infections.
desc_b: A large standardized metal box used for transporting goods by ship, rail, or truck.
rationale: A pharmaceutical substance is unrelated to a cargo transport container.

desc_a: An elaborate musical composition for full orchestra, typically in four movements.
desc_b: An official form used to declare income and calculate tax liability to a government authority.
rationale: A musical composition is unrelated to a fiscal government filing.

desc_a: A slowly moving mass of ice formed by accumulation and compaction of snow on mountains or polar regions.
desc_b: A formal request submitted by a candidate seeking employment at an organization.
rationale: A natural ice formation is unrelated to an employment-seeking document.

desc_a: A qualified practitioner of medicine who diagnoses and treats illness.
desc_b: A person legally qualified to represent clients in legal matters and act on their behalf.
rationale: Both are licensed professional roles requiring advanced training, giving moderate semantic proximity, but they denote genuinely distinct professions (medicine vs law).

desc_a: A person who plays a musical instrument or composes music, especially professionally.
desc_b: A person who is proficient in sports and physical exercise, especially competitively.
rationale: Both are skilled-performer professional roles with public recognition, but distinct domains (art vs sport).

desc_a: A liquid intended for drinking, other than plain water, such as juice or wine.
desc_b: A substance suitable for eating as food or used as an ingredient in cooking.
rationale: Both belong to the broader consumables domain, giving moderate similarity, but drinks and solid food are distinct sub-concepts in most taxonomies.

desc_a: A machine capable of flight, such as an airplane or helicopter, used to transport people or goods through the air.
desc_b: A vehicle or vessel designed to travel on or through water, such as a boat or ship.
rationale: Both are transportation-craft categories with structural naming similarity, but denote distinct modes of transport (air vs water).

desc_a: A person who writes novels, works of extended fictional prose narrative.
desc_b: A person who writes for newspapers, magazines, or news websites, reporting on current events.
rationale: Both are professional writers, giving moderate proximity, but fiction authorship and news reporting are distinct occupations.

desc_a: A passenger car with a separate trunk and a closed body typically seating four or more people.
desc_b: A two-wheeled motor vehicle that the rider straddles, typically without an enclosed cabin.
rationale: Both are motor road vehicles giving moderate lexical/semantic similarity, but a sedan and a motorcycle are distinct vehicle types, not interchangeable in most taxonomies.

desc_a: A facility where outpatients receive medical treatment or advice from healthcare professionals.
desc_b: A retail establishment where prescription and over-the-counter medicines are dispensed and sold.
rationale: Both are healthcare-adjacent physical premises, but a clinic (treatment site) and a pharmacy (medicine retailer) are distinct organizational types.

desc_a: A person or entity that commits capital to an asset with the expectation of a financial return.
desc_b: A person or entity that provides funds to another party with the expectation of repayment, typically with interest.
rationale: Both are capital-providing financial roles, but investing (equity/risk-sharing) and lending (debt/repayment) are structurally distinct financial relationships.

desc_a: A newly established business, typically small and in its initial phase, often aiming for rapid growth.
desc_b: A company in its initial phase of operation, still developing its product, market, or funding base.
rationale: Both describe a young, initial-phase business entity; different phrasing of the same real-world concept.

desc_a: A business that designs, engineers, and manufactures automobiles for sale.
desc_b: A business that designs, produces, and sells cars.
rationale: Same referent business type described with formal vs informal vocabulary.

desc_a: An organization that uses surplus revenue to further its stated mission rather than distributing it as profit.
desc_b: An organization set up to provide help or raise money for those in need, typically funded by donations.
rationale: In most everyday taxonomies these denote the same mission-driven, non-distributing organization concept.

desc_a: The highest-ranking executive in a company, responsible for overall management decisions.
desc_b: Chief Executive Officer, the top-ranking executive responsible for managing a company's overall operations.
rationale: Full title vs common acronym referring to the identical corporate role.

desc_a: A company that designs and produces smartphones for consumer use.
desc_b: A company that designs and produces mobile electronic devices such as phones and tablets.
rationale: Near-identical business category described at slightly different phrasing granularity, functionally the same concept for most extraction purposes.

desc_a: A business entity formed by lawyers to provide legal advice and representation to clients.
desc_b: A professional practice providing legal advice and representation to clients.
rationale: Different phrasing describing the identical professional-services organization concept.

desc_a: The combining of two or more companies into a single new entity.
desc_b: The process of combining multiple companies or business units into a unified, larger entity.
rationale: Different register (colloquial vs formal financial term) for the same business-combination event.

desc_a: A small timepiece worn on a strap or bracelet around the wrist.
desc_b: A small timepiece worn on a strap or bracelet around the wrist.
rationale: Compound vs spaced spelling of the same word/concept.

desc_a: A digital message sent electronically over a computer network.
desc_b: A digital message sent electronically over a computer network.
rationale: Hyphenated vs unhyphenated spelling variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A young human being, informally referred to.
desc_b: Young human beings, informally referred to.
rationale: Plural variant of the same informal person-concept.

desc_a: A business that sells or licenses software products to customers.
desc_b: A business that develops and sells software products.
rationale: Both describe a business whose core offering is software; near-synonymous business-type framing.

desc_a: The identification of a disease or condition based on symptoms and examination.
desc_b: A health problem, illness, or disorder affecting the body or mind.
rationale: Both are healthcare-domain concepts giving moderate lexical proximity, but a diagnosis (an identification act/label) is distinct from a medical condition (the underlying health state itself).

desc_a: A permit or ticket allowing entry to a place or event.
desc_b: Permits or tickets allowing entry to a place or event.
rationale: Plural variant of the same access-permit concept.

desc_a: A course of instruction in a particular subject, typically held at a set time and place.
desc_b: Courses of instruction in a particular subject, typically held at a set time and place.
rationale: Plural variant of the same instructional-session concept, in the education sense.

desc_a: A branch of an armed force or a body of people organized for a particular purpose, such as the Peace Corps.
desc_b: Informal abbreviation of 'corporation', a large business entity.
rationale: 'Corps' (organized body, especially military) is unrelated to 'Corp' (abbreviation for corporation); homophone/near-spelling trap yielding distinct concepts.

desc_a: Straps worn over the shoulders to hold up trousers.
desc_b: In British English, a strap attached to a garter belt to hold up stockings; a distinct single garment accessory.
rationale: Regional-sense divergence: 'suspenders' (US: trouser straps, plural-only noun) vs 'suspender' (UK: singular stocking-strap accessory) denote different garments; naive singularization crosses concept boundary.

desc_a: A structured group of people working toward a common purpose.
desc_b: A structured group of people working toward a common purpose.
rationale: British vs American spelling variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A person employed for wages or salary by an organization or another individual.
desc_b: Persons employed for wages or salary by an organization or another individual.
rationale: Singular/plural form of the same concept.

desc_a: A good or item manufactured or refined for sale.
desc_b: Goods or items manufactured or refined for sale.
rationale: Plural variant of the same concept, capitalized form.

desc_a: An act of assistance or work done for another, especially as a commercial offering.
desc_b: Acts of assistance or work done for another, especially as commercial offerings.
rationale: Plural variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A specific place or position in physical space.
desc_b: a specific place or position in physical space.
rationale: Case-only variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A style or method of cooking, especially as characteristic of a particular country or region.
desc_b: Any nourishing substance eaten or drunk to sustain life and growth.
rationale: In many entity-type taxonomies both collapse to the broader edible-substance/culinary concept; zero shared lexical tokens.

desc_a: A strong feeling of suitability for a particular career or occupation, often regarded as a calling.
desc_b: A person's regular work or profession, especially as a means of earning a living.
rationale: Near-synonymous concepts for a person's line of work; zero shared lexical tokens.

desc_a: A poor state of health; a period of sickness affecting the body or mind.
desc_b: A disorder of structure or function in an organism, especially one with a specific cause and recognizable signs.
rationale: Near-synonymous health-condition concepts, commonly collapsed in extraction taxonomies.

desc_a: A person who provides instruction or education, especially in a professional capacity.
desc_b: A person who imparts knowledge or skill to students.
rationale: Near-synonymous roles for a person who educates others; formal vs common register.

desc_a: A person or company that sells goods or services.
desc_b: A person or company that provides goods or services to another business.
rationale: Near-synonymous commercial roles referring to a party that furnishes goods or services.

desc_a: A written law passed by a legislative body.
desc_b: A rule enacted or customary in a community and recognized as binding by that community.
rationale: A statute is a formally enacted instance of law; both collapse to the same legal-rule concept in most extraction contexts.

desc_a: A medical practitioner qualified to perform surgery.
desc_b: A person licensed to practice medicine and treat patients.
rationale: A surgeon is a specialization of the broader medical-doctor concept; commonly collapsed in coarse-grained taxonomies.

desc_a: A two-wheeled vehicle propelled by pedaling, steered with handlebars.
desc_b: An informal term for a two-wheeled pedal-powered vehicle.
rationale: Formal vs informal register for the identical pedal-vehicle concept.

desc_a: A book used for the study of a particular subject, especially in schools or universities.
desc_b: A book designed for use by students following a particular course of study.
rationale: Near-synonymous educational-material concepts, zero shared lexical tokens.

desc_a: A large building used for storing goods before distribution or sale.
desc_b: A building or site designed to hold goods or materials for a period of time.
rationale: Near-synonymous concepts describing a goods-holding building; minor lexical overlap in description only, not in entity labels.

desc_a: A skilled performer of music, especially one who performs professionally at concerts and public events.
desc_b: A person who competes in organized sport at a professional or semi-professional level.
rationale: Both are publicly-recognized skilled-performer professional roles giving moderate similarity, but music performance and athletic competition are distinct domains.

desc_a: A liquid, other than plain water, prepared and consumed for refreshment or nourishment, such as tea or juice.
desc_b: Any solid substance grown or prepared for consumption as nourishment.
rationale: Both fall under the broader consumables domain giving moderate proximity, but liquid drinks and solid food are distinct sub-concepts in most taxonomies.

desc_a: A vehicle capable of atmospheric flight, including airplanes, helicopters, and gliders.
desc_b: A vessel or craft designed to travel across or beneath the surface of water.
rationale: Both are engineered transport craft giving structural similarity, but air travel and water travel are distinct transportation modes.

desc_a: A person who writes poetry, using rhythmic and often figurative language to express ideas and emotions.
desc_b: A person who writes novels, works of extended fictional prose narrative.
rationale: Both are literary-author professions giving moderate similarity, but poetry and novel writing are distinct literary forms and crafts.

desc_a: A medical practitioner who performs operations to treat injuries, diseases, or deformities of the body.
desc_b: A healthcare professional who diagnoses and treats conditions of the teeth, gums, and mouth.
rationale: Both are licensed healthcare professionals performing hands-on procedures, giving moderate similarity, but general surgery and dentistry are distinct specialties.

desc_a: A stringed musical instrument played with a bow, held under the chin, producing a high-pitched tone.
desc_b: A large stringed musical instrument played with a bow, held between the knees, producing a low-pitched tone.
rationale: Both are bowed string instruments in the same instrument family, giving moderate similarity, but they are distinct instruments with different size and range.

desc_a: An elected member of a legislative senate, responsible for making and voting on laws at a national or state level.
desc_b: An elected or appointed official who serves as the head of a state or provincial government.
rationale: Both are elected government officials giving moderate similarity, but a legislator and a chief executive of a state are structurally distinct political roles.

desc_a: Single-celled microorganisms that can exist independently and may cause disease.
desc_b: A submicroscopic infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of a host organism.
rationale: Both are microscopic disease-causing agents giving moderate biological-domain similarity, but bacteria and viruses are structurally and biologically distinct entities.

desc_a: A work of art created by applying pigment to a surface such as canvas, paper, or wood.
desc_b: A three-dimensional work of art created by carving, modeling, or casting.
rationale: Both are visual-art forms giving moderate similarity, but two-dimensional painting and three-dimensional sculpture are distinct artistic media.

desc_a: A small establishment selling light meals and beverages, such as coffee.
desc_b: A small establishment selling light meals and beverages, such as coffee.
rationale: Diacritic-only variant (é vs e) of the same concept.

desc_a: A document summarizing a person's education, skills, and work experience for job applications.
desc_b: A document summarizing a person's education, skills, and work experience for job applications.
rationale: Diacritic-only variant (é vs e) of the same concept.

desc_a: A style of visual art created by artists without formal training, characterized by simplicity and directness.
desc_b: A style of visual art created by artists without formal training, characterized by simplicity and directness.
rationale: Diacritic-only variant (ï vs i) of the same concept.

desc_a: A commercial business entity that produces or sells goods and services.
desc_b: A commercial business entity that produces or sells goods and services.
rationale: All-caps vs title-case variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A device that produces X-ray radiation for medical imaging or industrial inspection.
desc_b: A device that produces X-ray radiation for medical imaging or industrial inspection.
rationale: Casing variant on the internal hyphenated segment (X-Ray vs X-ray) of the same concept.

desc_a: A probabilistic machine learning classifier based on applying Bayes' theorem with strong independence assumptions.
desc_b: A probabilistic machine learning classifier based on applying Bayes' theorem with strong independence assumptions.
rationale: Combined diacritic (ï vs i) and leading-case variant of the same concept.

desc_a: A legal advisor who represents or advises a person or organization on legal matters.
desc_b: A person who practices law, representing and advising clients on legal matters.
rationale: Near-synonymous legal-advisor roles; zero shared lexical tokens between 'counsel' and 'lawyer'.
